outcome: an agent iterates a wheeled robot's control to a numeric target it cannot hit first try
status: PRE-FREEZE. Nothing here is a result. The pilot is n=1 and exploratory (loopbench-plan.md section 5).
achieved_rule: reached at least once (solved_at_least_once); never quotable as a pass rate at n=1

container.shared_with: T1_arrive -- the SAME three description files, deliberately. L2 is not a harder scene, it is a tighter target plus a loop. Reusing T1's container means the ladder's achievability floor already covers the asset, so an L2 failure cannot be the robot's fault.

robot.note: The name the robot description declares. Resolution is the ladder's: the declared name first, then a unique mass match.

waypoint.resolution_rule: goal_xy = the graded body's horizontal position at the FIRST recorded sample + offset_m, exactly as T1 resolves it.

constants_note: ARRIVE_TOL_M and SETTLE_DEADLINE_S are set from a MEASURED sweep on the omnisim column (2026-08-02, machine 9722d23d12a3, ODE), recorded in loopbench-l2-calibration.md: the obvious first attempt returns 0.0997 m / 13.57 s and fails BOTH clauses, while a tuned control returns 0.0495 m / 8.08 s and clears both. The deadline is 9.0 s rather than 8.0 s so the demonstrated solution has ~0.9 s of margin and the rung measures iteration rather than luck. Six cold runs of the tuned control returned those two numbers to four decimals, so the margin is not noise. FROZEN: a threshold that moves after measurement is worthless whichever way it moves.

harness.why: L2 is graded from the standalone cold re-run plus the session transcript. The agent may use any live surface it likes to close its loop -- that is the point of the rung -- but the VERDICT never comes from the agent's own session.

expectation.omnisim: achievable; the target was demonstrated by a scripted control before this file was written
expectation.mujoco: achievable; MuJoCo can drive this URDF and measure its own state directly
expectation.discriminator: NOT whether the target is hit -- both columns should manage that -- but what the loop COSTS: how many tool calls, how much wall clock, and how many lines of glue the column needed before an agent could measure its own result at all.
expectation.pre_registered_risk: If both columns close the loop with comparable cost, L2 is NOT_DISCRIMINATING and is cut (loopbench-plan.md section 5, outcome 5). That is a live possibility: MuJoCo in-process state access is a genuinely strong way to close a loop.

cost_class: CPU minutes. No GPU. Tokens only.
